reviewer_scope: The experiment author reviewed only sealed public before observations and exact legal menus. Arm choices, arm scores, forecast probabilities and later outcomes were hidden until this file was written and hashed.

cases.assessment: Two connected settlement sites exist. Trading the four-sheep surplus for brick shifts the missing settlement resource to sheep, produced on 8 and 12, while brick arrives only on 11.
One connected settlement site exists. Sheep-for-wood changes the shortage from wood on 10 to sheep on 8 or 12; brick and wheat are already held.
Two connected settlement sites exist. Brick is absent from hand and visible own production; wood-for-brick spends a surplus replenished on 9 to open a settlement route.
At a known eight points with one connected settlement site, sheep-for-brick opens a settlement after sheep production on 6 or 10. Sheep-for-ore also starts a city route with ore production on 6.
The same one-site brick shortage persists with extra wheat. A brick trade points toward settlement; an ore trade could pair with the visible two-ore roll on 6 for a city.
One connected settlement site exists. Wood and ore are absent from own production; wheat-for-wood directly supports a settlement, while wheat is produced on 3, 4 and 5.
No settlement pieces remain, so city is the current point route. Wheat-for-ore completes the ore requirement and can refill wheat from visible 3, 4 and 5 production.
Two upgradeable settlements exist and ore is absent from own production. Wheat-for-ore makes the city ore requirement while visible wheat production can refill the spent wheat.
The same city ore shortage remains after a robber move removes one brick source. Wheat-for-ore still uses visible wheat production to complete the city route.
At known eight points with one connected settlement site, brick is absent from hand and available only on 5. Wheat-for-brick shifts the remaining deficit to abundant wheat production.
At known eight points, ore is plentiful but wheat is absent. Ore-for-wheat supports a city while retaining enough ore after one visible 8 production; settlement needs several other resources.
One connected settlement site exists. Brick is absent from hand and own production; wheat-for-brick uses a four-wheat surplus backed by visible 3 and 10 production.
